{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Short-lived high-volume Bernoulli bandits with bounded-density priors\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{ONX\_\allowbreak{}SHORT\_\allowbreak{}LIVED\_\allowbreak{}HIGH\_\allowbreak{}VOLUME\_\allowbreak{}BERNOULLI}



Online learning and bandits



Long-run Bayesian average loss with random arriving arms, finite lifetimes, and entire-round batched feedback.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap



\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Short lived bayesian bandit; task family: Online bandit



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Stochastic bernoulli; operation: Batched bernoulli rewards; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared



\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} randomization: Private randomness allowed



\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} quantifier: Algorithm before instance



\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} measure: Arrivals per round; measure: Lifetime; measure: Plays per round



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Minimize long-run Bayesian average loss relative to the best currently alive arm in a streaming short-lived high-volume bandit.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


At the start of every calendar round t, a new disjoint cohort A\_t of k arms arrives. An arm born at t remains available through t+w inclusive. Thus there are w+1 alive cohorts after initialization and w useful feedback opportunities before its last allocation.



Each arm mean is drawn independently from a distribution D on [0,1]. Conditional on all means, rewards are independent Bernoulli draws across arms and plays. The prior density satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{c_1\le f(u)\le c_2} almost everywhere, where \AtlasInlineMath{0<c_1\le1\le c_2<\infty}. Arrival identities and times contain no mean information. The parameters w,c\_1,c\_2 are fixed for the rate statements.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


At each round the policy chooses nonnegative integer allocations \AtlasInlineMath{\pi_t(a)} to alive arms, with \AtlasInlineMath{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\pi_t(a)=n}. The entire allocation is measurable before any reward from that round is revealed. All rewards from these n plays are revealed together afterward; no within-round adaptation or stopping is permitted.



The values n,k,w,c\_1,c\_2 are public. The policy may be given D; the upper policy uses only its density bounds, and the lower bound holds even when D is the known uniform prior. The arm means are hidden.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


The output is the executed sequence of batch allocations. Exactly n plays must be assigned each round, always to arms that are alive.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}


Let \AtlasInlineMath{\mu_t^*=\max_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\mu_a}. For a finite evaluation horizon T, \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal L_{n,T}(\pi;D)=(nT)^{-1}\mathbb E_D\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\pi_t(a)(\mu_t^*-\mu_a)}. The expectation includes the prior, rewards, and policy randomness.



The long-run risk uses \AtlasInlineMath{\overline{\mathcal L}_n(\pi;D)=\limsup_{T\to\infty}\mathcal L_{n,T}(\pi;D)}. Define \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal L_n^*(c_1,c_2)=\inf_\pi\sup_{D\in\mathfrak D(c_1,c_2)}\overline{\mathcal L}_n(\pi;D)}, allowing a policy to take D as input. The expectation precedes the limit superior; this is not an expectation-of-limsup criterion.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


The resource parameters are n plays per calendar round, k arriving arms per round, and lifetime w+1 rounds. There are nT rewards over a finite T-round evaluation. The asymptotic rate sends n to infinity at fixed w,c\_1,c\_2, with k possibly depending on n; T is sent to infinity inside the long-run performance criterion.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


All randomized policies with allocations measurable before current-round feedback are allowed. Arms may be sampled multiple times in a round, but allocations cannot adapt within that round. The prior may be known.




\AtlasMath{\sup_{D\in\mathfrak D(c_1,c_2)}\limsup_{T\to\infty}\mathcal L_{n,T}(\pi;D)\le\ell}




One upper policy depending only on n,k,w,c\_1,c\_2 handles every density in the class. The lower bound holds for every policy under the fixed known uniform prior and even for liminf of the finite-horizon expected losses.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_per\_round\_play\_count



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}


\AtlasInlineMath{n}: Number of plays allocated in every round \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{n\ge1} integer.



\AtlasInlineMath{k}: Number of newly arriving arms each round \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{k\ge1} integer.



\AtlasInlineMath{w}: Number of feedback opportunities before an arm final-age allocation \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{w\ge1} integer; lifespan is w+1 rounds.



\AtlasInlineMath{c_1,c_2}: Prior density lower and upper bounds \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<c_1\le1\le c_2<\infty}.



\AtlasInlineMath{D}: Prior distribution of independent arm means \textbf{Domain:} Density between c\_1 and c\_2 on [0,1].



\AtlasInlineMath{T}: Finite evaluation horizon before the long-run limit \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{T\ge1} integer.



\AtlasInlineMath{\alpha_w}: Optimal finite-lifetime exponent \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<\alpha_w<1/2}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\alpha_w=(2^w-1)/(2^{w+1}-1)}



\AtlasInlineMath{\rho}: Fixed polynomial arrival exponent \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\rho>0}.



\AtlasInlineMath{k=\lfloor n^\rho\rfloor} in the polynomial-arrival regime



\AtlasInlineMath{n_0}: Source asymptotic threshold \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{n_0=n_0(w,c_1,c_2)} finite.



\needspace{12\baselineskip}\section{3. Complexity bracket}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Compared quantities}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Q1 - minimax metric resource quantity}


\AtlasMath{\mathcal L_n^*(c_1,c_2)}


\textbf{Scope.} The union of the explicit parameter and dimension domains of the linked comparison regimes; each bound retains its own applicability conditions.



\textbf{Optimization direction.} minimize



\textbf{Resource contract.} expression: \AtlasInlineMath{(n,k,w)}; description: Exactly n plays per round, k arrivals per round, and a fixed finite lifetime.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{R1 - Finite lifetime with arbitrary arrival count}


\textbf{Region.} Fix integer \AtlasInlineMath{w\ge1} and \AtlasInlineMath{0<c_1\le1\le c_2<\infty}; require \AtlasInlineMath{n\ge n_0(w,c_1,c_2)} and any integer \AtlasInlineMath{k\ge1}. No ambient Euclidean dimension; the number of alive arms is at most k(w+1). The lower bound is for liminf of expected averages, hence also bounds the same limsup-risk used by the upper bound.



\textbf{Quantity.} Q1



\textbf{Resource.} Exactly n plays per round, k arrivals per round, and a fixed finite lifetime.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap



\textbf{Lower bound.} B2



\AtlasMath{\Omega_w(\max\{k^{-1},n^{-\alpha_w}\})}


\textbf{Upper bound.} B1



\AtlasMath{O_{w,c_1,c_2}\!\left(\min\{1,(\log n)/k+((\log n)/n)^{\alpha_w}\}\right)}


\textbf{Gap or comparison.} At most logarithmic factors in n; max and sum of the two positive scales differ only by a factor of two.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{R2 - Optimal exponent for polynomial arm arrivals}


\textbf{Region.} Fix \AtlasInlineMath{w,c_1,c_2} as above and \AtlasInlineMath{\rho>0}; let \AtlasInlineMath{k=\lfloor n^\rho\rfloor} and \AtlasInlineMath{n\ge n_0} sufficiently large. Alive-arm count grows as (w+1)floor(n\textasciicircum{}rho); no Euclidean dimension.



\textbf{Quantity.} Q1



\textbf{Resource.} Per-round n, polynomial k, and fixed w; the performance is a long-run average.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap



\textbf{Lower bound.} B4



\AtlasMath{\widetilde\Omega_{w,\rho}(n^{-\min\{\rho,\alpha_w\}})}


\textbf{Upper bound.} B3



\AtlasMath{\widetilde O_{w,c_1,c_2,\rho}(n^{-\min\{\rho,\alpha_w\}})}


\textbf{Gap or comparison.} The polynomial exponent is matched; only logarithmic factors remain.
